elements.scope_reason: Re-assessment trigger while awaiting transport (BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, RR > 20 or < 9, SpO2 < 94%, drop in GCS). It reads as management (reassess ABC), but it is also an escalation criterion: the briefing names 'BP < 90/60 with altered consciousness' as an Emergency example.
elements.problem: No rule encodes these vital-sign thresholds (no escalation above Urgent for an injured patient with deteriorating vitals). Only the shock footnote's different thresholds (SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30) appear.

elements.scope_reason: Same-day referral criteria for an injured patient not needing urgent attention (pregnant, bleeding disorder, anticoagulant, high-speed collision, ejected/hit by vehicle, fall > 3 m) are triage logic but sit below the red box; the briefing only mandates the red box as Urgent.
elements.problem: No priority rule (e.g. a lower level such as Priority/same-day) captures these mechanism and risk-factor criteria.

'If mild headache, dizziness or mental fogginess, concussion likely' -> probable Concussion with head-injury trigger and 'or'. Dizziness is not in any check_for (fine only if it counts as a common symptom).

summary: Red-box criteria are largely captured faithfully in four Urgent priority rules plus probable shock and concussion rules, with careful touches (> 2 ribs enumerated from three upward, finding_site for head/chest penetrating wounds). The most consequential defects: open fracture encoded with a morphologic-abnormality concept instead of the 'Open fracture' disorder, 'vomiting ≥ 2 times' collapsed to any vomiting, 'muscle tightness' and 'pale' dropped, and the vital-sign deterioration thresholds at the foot of the red box not encoded.
